cards.front: What should discovery capture before you choose a pattern or model?
cards.back: Business goal, users and workflow, data sources, latency, volume/cost, compliance and risk, failure tolerance, and **success metrics with how they will be measured**.

cards.front: The four properties of good success criteria in Anthropic's eval docs?
cards.back: **Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant.** They are usually multidimensional; the docs list task fidelity, consistency, relevance and coherence, tone and style, privacy preservation, context utilization, latency and price.

cards.front: Why agree on success metrics before design?
cards.back: They become the eval suite, define "done", and give an objective way to settle later trade-off disputes.

cards.front: Best single discovery artifact for an LLM project?
cards.back: A set of **real example inputs with expected outputs**. It seeds the eval set and exposes edge cases interviews miss.

cards.front: Why record non-goals ("v1 will not issue refunds")?
cards.back: They are requirements: they shrink scope and the tool surface (supporting least privilege) and prevent scope creep.

cards.front: Team picks a multi-agent framework before any metric exists. Defensible next step?
cards.back: Go back to discovery: define the goal, constraints and measurable success criteria. Then choose the **simplest** pattern that meets them.

cards.front: Which discovery answers decide sync API vs Message Batches?
cards.back: Latency (does someone wait?) and volume/cost. Overnight or bulk work with no one waiting points to batches; blocking or interactive work stays synchronous.

cards.front: Three things every option you present must state
cards.back: Its **cost, risk and benefit**, in business terms (cost per task, SLA impact, time to value, auditability).

cards.front: How many options in a decision presentation, and against what?
cards.back: Two to four **credible** alternatives, scored against the criteria agreed in discovery, with an explicit recommendation.

cards.front: Parts of a lightweight architecture decision record (ADR)
cards.back: Context, options considered, decision, consequences (including new work), sign-offs, and a **revisit trigger**.

cards.front: Which stakeholders should sign off on tool scope and data flows?
cards.back: Security (tool scope, credentials, least privilege) and legal/compliance (data flow, retention). Product signs off on the trade-off; operations on the support burden.

cards.front: Compliance sign-off should be based on the contract or the data flow?
cards.back: The **actual data flow**. Governance follows where data really goes.

cards.front: A stakeholder demands a guaranteed behaviour. Right response?
cards.back: Enforce it in code, a workflow gate or a schema, and explain that. Do not promise a stronger prompt will guarantee it.

cards.front: How to communicate non-determinism honestly?
cards.back: Quote eval results (e.g. % correct / declined / wrong on N cases) and describe the error types, rather than "very accurate".

cards.front: Executive asks "why not just use the biggest model?"
cards.back: Show eval results and cost per task by model tier. Often a smaller model plus better retrieval or prompts meets the bar for less.

cards.front: Message Batches API: discount and completion window
cards.back: **50%** off input and output tokens; asynchronous; most batches finish in under an hour, but processing is capped at **24 hours**: results are released when all requests finish or at 24 h, whichever is first, and unfinished requests **expire** (not billed; resubmit them). Results downloadable for 29 days.

cards.front: Can you promise real-time or one-hour turnaround on a batch pipeline?
cards.back: No. Batches have no per-request latency guarantee and processing can take up to 24 h. Blocking or interactive paths stay on the synchronous API.

cards.front: SLA arithmetic for a batch pipeline
cards.back: Worst case = wait for next submission + up to 24 h processing + your own processing and retries. The submission interval must leave headroom inside the SLA.

cards.front: SLA of 36 h using batches: roughly how often must you submit?
cards.back: Well under every 12 h (36 − 24), with buffer for retries and processing, e.g. every 6 to 8 h.

cards.front: SLO vs SLA
cards.back: SLO = internal target you engineer to; SLA = external commitment, set with headroom below what the SLO shows you can deliver.

cards.front: What can be guaranteed vs only measured in an LLM system?
cards.back: Guaranteed: output format (structured outputs / tool schemas), rules enforced in code or gates. Measured: judgement, tone, correctness rates.

cards.front: What should happen to every confirmed production failure?
cards.back: It becomes a **new eval case** before or alongside the fix, so it cannot silently regress.

cards.front: Richer feedback signals than star ratings
cards.back: Reviewer edits, human overrides, escalations and support tickets, captured where work already happens.

cards.front: The system is missing its SLA for one input type. Best move?
cards.back: Show the data, offer options with costs (human review, stronger model for that segment, re-scoped target), let the business owner choose, and record the decision.

cards.front: LLM-specific items an architecture doc must record
cards.back: Exact model IDs and last eval date, prompt versions with eval scores, tool inventory with permissions, known limitations, eval suite location and thresholds.

cards.front: Structure of a useful runbook entry
cards.back: Symptom, likely cause, check, fix, escalation, and a **do-not** line warning against the tempting wrong fix.

cards.front: Answers cite last quarter's policy after an upload. First check?
cards.back: Retrieval: is the index refreshed? The model is answering faithfully from stale retrieved text. Do not swap models first.

cards.front: Where do team-wide Claude Code conventions belong?
cards.back: Committed project `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/` and shared `.claude/skills/`, **not** a user-level `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or a wiki.

cards.front: Conventions for test files scattered across many folders?
cards.back: `.claude/rules/*.md` with `paths:` globs (e.g. `**/*.test.ts`); they load when Claude reads a matching file.

cards.front: Repeatable procedure such as "add a new tool" or "run evals"?
cards.back: A **skill** (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`), loaded on demand.

cards.front: Do CLAUDE.md instructions enforce rules?
cards.back: No, they guide. Must-always rules belong in hooks, CI checks or permission rules.

cards.front: How to test a handoff pack?
cards.back: Have someone outside the build team handle a staged incident using only the runbook; each blocker is a documentation bug.

cards.front: The five lifecycle phases in task 6.5
cards.back: Discovery, design, handoff, monitoring, iteration.

cards.front: What connects every lifecycle phase?
cards.back: The **eval suite**: seeded in discovery, used to choose in design, handed over as the definition of "working", mirrored in monitoring, and gating every iteration.

cards.front: LLM-specific monitoring signals
cards.back: Sampled output quality, human override/escalation rate, input drift, tokens per task, stop reasons (e.g. `max_tokens`) and tool errors.

cards.front: Claude model lifecycle states
cards.back: **Active, Legacy, Deprecated, Retired.** Requests to a retired model fail.

cards.front: Minimum notice Anthropic gives before retiring a publicly released model
cards.back: **At least 60 days.** Partner platforms (Bedrock, Google Cloud) set their own schedules.

cards.front: Your model is deprecated. Defensible plan?
cards.back: Run the full eval suite on the recommended replacement well before retirement, compare quality/latency/cost, roll out gradually, and inform stakeholders.

cards.front: Why pin exact model IDs in production?
cards.back: So behaviour changes only through a deliberate, evaluated release, and the model register shows what to re-test when deprecations are announced.

cards.front: What does a good handoff transfer besides documents?
cards.back: Named ownership, working tooling (eval runner, dashboards, CLAUDE.md/rules/skills), a drill, and an agreed support window.
